# TODO

The single task file. Every agent, the swarm orchestrator and the integrator read and write only this file for task state.

| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[ ]` | Open. Nobody has taken it. |
| `[-]` | Taken. An agent is working it (`agent:` names who). |
| `[x]` | Done. Evidence and the PR or commit are on the entry. |

Rules for agents:
- Pick the first open task whose `depends` are all done. Change `[ ]` to `[-]` and add `- agent: <your name>` before you start. Keep WIP one per agent.
- When the task passes every gate, change it to `[x]`, add `- evidence:` (commands, CI run, SHA) and `- pr:` in the same change. Never mark `[x]` without evidence.
- If you stop without finishing, put the mark back to `[ ]` and remove `agent:`.
- Swarm workers do not edit this file. The orchestrator marks `[-]` when it starts a worker and the integrator marks `[x]` when it merges. A task is swarm-dispatchable when it has a `scope`.
- Entry fields: `requirements`, `depends` (task IDs), `scope` (comma-separated path prefixes), `reserved` (one database migration version), `aliases`, `agent`, `pr`, `evidence`, `details` (indented text). Specification requirement IDs come from SMARTCLINIC_V1_SPEC.md.
- Name folders and Java packages after the business domain (for example `capacity`, `events`, `patient.identity`), never after a task, story or gate ID such as `s_g5_05` or `x_01`: a task's `scope` is where its files go, so never write an ID-based path there. `scripts/check-names.py` fails the build on any new one.
- Add new stories, acceptance changes and improvement ideas here as new `[ ]` entries. Record defects in BUGS.md.
- Automatic sections: `## Repairs (automatic)` holds `FIX-<run>` repairs of a red `main`, `## Audit findings` holds the daily audit's `AUD-` tasks, and `## Issue fixes` holds `ISS-<n>` tasks made from GitHub issue #n by the issue monitor. `attempts` counts worker runs; at 3 a task waits (the issue monitor may give it one more round).

Simulated review findings are evidence of review activity, not clinical or human pilot acceptance. Real-patient approval remains a G5 gate.

## Instructions for every agent (read this first)

You are one worker on the SmartClinic V1 team. Follow these steps in order for every task. Do not skip a step because the task looks small.

1. **Read the rules before you touch code.** Read these files completely, in this order: `AGENTS.md`, `CODING_STYLE.md`, `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, `docs/SWARM.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `WORKSPACE.md`. Then read `SMARTCLINIC_V1_SPEC.md`: the sections named in your task's `requirements`, plus section 7 (architecture) and section 8 and 8.1 (security, operations, production web platform). Read every file under `docs/decisions/`. For staff web or patient app work also read `docs/design/README.md`, `docs/design/screens-and-navigation.md`, `docs/design/screen-recipe.md`, `docs/design/token-contract.md`, `docs/design/accessibility-patterns.md` and `docs/design/rtl-and-localization.md`. For database work read `db/migrations/README.md`; for API contracts read `contracts/README.md`.
2. **Load the skill for your area.** The skills are in `.opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Always load `smartclinic-delivery`. Then load the ones that match the files you change: Java and Spring `smartclinic-senior-backend`, security and login `smartclinic-senior-spring-security`, database `smartclinic-senior-database`, build and tests `smartclinic-senior-java-build` and `smartclinic-test-engineer`, web `smartclinic-senior-react` and `smartclinic-senior-typescript`, mobile `smartclinic-senior-mobile`, shell `smartclinic-senior-shell`, Python `smartclinic-senior-python`, CI and infrastructure `smartclinic-devsecops` and `smartclinic-senior-cloud-iac`, review `smartclinic-qa-reviewer`.
3. **Stay inside the task.** Change only files under the task's `scope`. If the task needs a file outside it, stop, write the reason in your notes file (the path in your prompt) under `## Why this is not finished`, and finish without changing that file.
4. **Write the failing test first**, then the smallest change that makes it pass, then clean up. Use synthetic data only. Never commit a secret, token, password, key, real patient data or a real domain name.
5. **Names.** Name folders, packages, classes and files after what they hold (business domain), never after a task, story or gate ID. `scripts/check-names.py` fails the build on `s_g5_05`, `x_04`, `dlv_02` and similar.
6. **Run the checks yourself** before you finish: `bash scripts/worker-check.sh` for API work, `bash apps/staff-web/check.sh` for staff web, `bash apps/patient-mobile/check.sh` for the patient app, `python3 -I scripts/check-docs.py` when you edit Markdown, and for any Java or script change also `python3 -I -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests` (it fails on an unqualified Javadoc `{@link}`, an ID-style name and similar). For any change to `scripts/*.py` also run `bash scripts/python-coverage.sh`: every line and branch you add or change must be covered by a test you add under `scripts/tests`, or it fails. All must pass. Paste the commands and their final lines into your notes file under `## Test evidence`, and the coverage result under `## Coverage` (AGENTS.md, Coverage rules and Swarm hand-off).
7. **Commits and pull requests.** Never add `Co-Authored-By` or `Claude-Session` lines to a commit message or pull request description.
8. **Do not edit `TODO.md`, `tasks/`, `.github/workflows/*`, `.opencode/*`, `opencode.json`, `AGENTS.md` or `scripts/*`.** The orchestrator, the integrator and people own them, and a pull request that touches them is not merged automatically. Put a lesson for these files under `## Lessons for workers` in your notes.
9. **If something is unclear or the spec and the task disagree**, do not guess. Write the question and what you found under `## Why this is not finished` in your notes file and stop. When your prompt has findings from earlier runs, start from them.

    Spec rule WEB-04. Counters live in memory per API instance; the edge WAF supplies the global limit (WEB-01). Say so in the class Javadoc.
    1. Create `web/RateLimiter.java`: a plain class with a constructor `(Clock clock, int perMinute)` and `long retryAfterSeconds(String key)` that returns 0 when the call is allowed and counts it, or the seconds until the current one-minute window ends when the key already used `perMinute` calls. Use a `ConcurrentHashMap<String, Window>`; evict windows older than two minutes on every call so memory cannot grow forever. A `Clock` bean already exists (`config/ClockConfiguration.java`).
    2. In `TenantContextInterceptor.preHandle`, right after `TenantContext.set(...)`, call the limiter with the key `organization + ":" + subject`. When it returns more than 0: set header `Retry-After` to that number and throw `new ApiException(429, "RATE_LIMITED", "too many requests")`. Read the limit from property `smartclinic.rate-limit.per-minute` (default 600) in `application.yml`.
    3. Tests in `RateLimiterTest` with a mutable fake `Clock`: the (limit+1)th call in a minute returns a positive value; the same key is allowed again after the window; two keys do not share a counter; old windows are evicted. Add one interceptor test that the 429 response has the `Retry-After` header.
    Do NOT add a library dependency, do NOT key by IP address, do NOT log the key.

    Problem (verified in `docs/decisions/0003-persistence-of-in-memory-stores.md`): `InMemoryFlowPolicyStore` is a `@Repository` that keeps all state in process memory, so every restart loses it and two API instances disagree. Replace it with PostgreSQL. This store owns migration V61 only.
    1. Read `messaging/flows/FlowPolicyStore.java` (the interface; every method already takes the organization id) and `InMemoryFlowPolicyStore.java` (the behaviour to copy) completely. Read `PatientFlowPresentationService.java` to see which methods production code calls. Read one existing JDBC repository for style (`patient/PatientRepository.java`) and `db/migrations/V58*.sql` plus one earlier migration that creates a tenant table, to copy how tables get `organization_id`, forced row-level security and the `public.app_org()` policy.
    2. Create `db/migrations/V61__flow_policies.sql` with one table per aggregate the interface stores (name them after the business concept, no story ids). Every table: `organization_id` not null, primary key including it where identifiers are only unique per tenant, `created_at timestamptz not null default now()`, `ENABLE` and `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, a policy `USING (organization_id = public.app_org())`, and GRANT to `smartclinic_app` exactly as the earlier migration does. Append-only facts get no UPDATE grant. The migration is additive only.
    3. Create `JdbcFlowPolicyStore` in the same package, `@Repository`, constructor-injected `JdbcTemplate`, parameterised SQL only, implementing every interface method with the same semantics (same exceptions, same empty results).
    4. Remove `@Repository` from `InMemoryFlowPolicyStore` and keep it only for unit tests (move it under `apps/api/src/test/java/com/aurevia/smartclinic/messaging/flows` if production code no longer uses it: `grep -rn InMemoryFlowPolicyStore apps/api/src/main`).
    5. Write `JdbcFlowPolicyStoreIntegrationTest` under `apps/api/src/test/java/com/aurevia/smartclinic/messaging/flows/it/` (tag `integration`; copy the setup of an existing class there): save then read back, update path if the interface has one, and tenant A cannot read tenant B rows with identical local ids.
    6. Run `bash scripts/worker-check.sh`. Also run the AUD-20261120-04 row-level-security gate if it exists.

## Platform build-out, part 6: durable storage

ADR 0003 (`docs/decisions/0003-persistence-of-in-memory-stores.md`) lists the adapters that still keep data in memory. Each task replaces one store with a PostgreSQL adapter, keeps the tenant (organization ID) in every key and in every query, and keeps the existing port unchanged. READY-37 to READY-42 cover the other stores. Production wiring must pick the JDBC adapter; the in-memory adapter stays for unit tests only.

- [ ] BUILD-67 · Reception worklist and check-in screen: match the approved design
  - requirements: CLN-01, CLN-02, UX-01
  - scope: apps/staff-web/src/features/scheduling
  - depends: BUILD-52
  - details:
    1. Read `features/scheduling` and `docs/design/screen-recipe.md`.
    2. Open the approved picture `docs/design/approved/reception-worklist.png` and match it. In words: A dark navigation column about 230 px wide on the left (Today is the active item; then Patients, Schedule, Messages with an unread badge, Finance; at the bottom the user's role, name and the idle-session countdown). The content sits on a light page background. At the top: the title Today, a line with the date, the facility name and its time zone, and on the right a facility select, a language switch (English and Arabic) and a primary New booking button. Under it a row of five equal white cards, one per state (label, large number, small note). Under that two columns: a wide white card with the worklist (a heading and three filter chips on top, then the table, then a footer with the row count and the last update time) and a narrow column (320 to 420 px) with two cards, Check-in and Booking check (the second holds an amber alert and three slot buttons). A state badge is a pill with a small dot and the state word: booked blue tint, checked in green tint, in progress amber tint, completed gray, no-show red tint; the word is always shown. When the screen is narrow the columns stack and the navigation moves to the top. Use design tokens, never raw colours. Touch targets are at least 44 px (48 px on the phone). Show state with a word or icon as well as colour.
    3. Today page: header with facility name and time zone, facility switcher and language switch; five state counts (booked, checked in, in progress, completed, no-show) with a note each; the worklist ordered by scheduled time with time, patient and MRN, visit type, clinician and room, state badge with time in state, assigned person and one action (Check in, Hand off, Open chart, Rebook). Filters: all, needs check-in, waiting over 15 minutes.
    4. Check-in panel: appointment summary, date of birth, language, identifier with issuer and verified state, self-pay balance, identity checklist, one button that records the checker, time and facility. Handoff needs an active assignee.
    5. Booking check: when a slot was just taken show an alert with the nearest free slots to pick from; nothing is booked twice.
    6. Tests: each state badge has text and not colour alone, the no-show action asks for a reason, the conflict alert appears on a stale slot, English and Arabic with the layout flipped.

## Pharmacy, laboratory and radiology workflows, plus order tracking (new files and narrow edits)

The clinician side is in ORDER-01 to ORDER-10. These tasks add the receiving sides and the links between them. PHARM: routed inbox, status events, clarification thread, substitution proposals the prescriber must approve, and plain patient status. LABFLOW: collection, rejection and recollection, result entry and verification with change checks, corrections and release, outage fallback and a turnaround board. RADFLOW: performing-site worklist and report or addendum delivery with acknowledgment. TRACK: one journey timeline, a patient 'where is it' tracker, a partner outage board, an end-to-end test and a care-loop diagram.

## Staff messaging: inside a facility and between facilities, instant and email-like, with attachments (new files and narrow edits)

The specification covers patient and care-unit messaging only (MSG-01 to MSG-07). Staff-to-staff messaging is new scope: SMSG-01 is a decision pack for a person to approve and amend the specification. The build tasks can run meanwhile because they follow the same rules as MSG-03 and MSG-07 (explicit send, scanned attachments, audit, retention, no identifiers in notifications). Messaging between different organizations stays off and refused until a person enables it.

- [-] SMSG-01 · Decision pack: staff messaging inside a facility and between facilities (spec amendment for a person to approve)
  - agent: swarm-6
  - attempts: 1
  - requirements: MSG-03, MSG-07, ARC-07
  - scope: docs/decisions/staff-messaging
  - details:
    1. Read the messaging requirements (MSG-01 to MSG-07, ARC-07) in `SMARTCLINIC_V1_SPEC.md`. They cover patient and care-unit conversations only; staff-to-staff messaging is new scope.
    2. Write `docs/decisions/staff-messaging/README.md`: the proposed requirement text (instant chat and email-like messages, inside a facility and between facilities, with attachments), what is out of scope (patient messaging, external email, voice), and the questions a person must answer: may facilities of different organizations message each other and under what agreement; retention and legal hold period; whether patient identifiers are allowed in message text; attachment size limit.
    3. Do NOT edit `SMARTCLINIC_V1_SPEC.md`: a person amends it. Say that plainly at the top of the file.

## Printing: prescriptions, lab and imaging orders, chart summary and reports for the patient (new files and narrow edits)

A physician can print a prescription, a lab or imaging order, a chart summary or a signed report for the patient. Only signed or placed items print; every print and reprint is audited. PRINT-01 to PRINT-03 are the API; PRINT-04 to PRINT-09 are the staff web; PRINT-10 to PRINT-12 are tests, the patient app and docs.

  - agent: swarm-8
  - attempts: 1
  - requirements: CLN-07, RX-02, LAB-01, RAD-01, ARC-06
  - scope: apps/api/src/main/java/com/aurevia/smartclinic/printing, apps/api/src/test/java/com/aurevia/smartclinic/printing
  - details:
    1. Read the `documents` package (`PdfBindingService`, `DocumentGuard`), `prescription`, `orders` and `chart` packages and the PDF clauses of `SMARTCLINIC_V1_SPEC.md` (CLN-07, ARC-06).

English or Arabic, embedded fonts, direction-aware layout, page numbers, A4, patient name and identifier, clinician and facility, issue time and a provenance footer.
    3. A prescription handout is produced only for a signed or attested prescription with an approved print channel (BUILD-10). An order handout only for an order that is placed, not draft. A chart summary or report only for signed content. Anything else returns a clear refusal.

## Frontend and design foundations (swarm tasks)

Independent modules scoped to their own paths so workers cannot collide with backend work.

## G1 — clinic

Gate evidence: competing bookings enforce one protected slot; stale drafts cannot overwrite signed records; corrections preserve the signed original; English and Arabic PDFs validated; consolidation is all-or-nothing.

- [ ] S-G1-09 · G1 gate evidence and Product Owner acceptance (G1).

## G2 — labs and exchange

Gate evidence: rejected or recollected specimens trace to the right order; duplicate and reordered events do not duplicate or overwrite final reports; unmatched results wait for review; critical results escalate on deadline with human acknowledgment, and corrections reopen review.

- [ ] S-G2-11 · G2 gate evidence and Product Owner acceptance (G2).

## G3 — patient and operations

Gate evidence: confirmed patients see only authorized revisions; generic notifications reveal no clinical detail; withdrawn releases stop future access; messaging works on both mobile platforms including wrong-unit denial, uploads, instructions, revision-specific acknowledgment, failed uploads, notification retry and revoked connections.

- [ ] S-G3-13 · G3 gate evidence and Product Owner acceptance (G3).

## G4 — specialty and finance

Gate evidence: wrong-patient study association refused; radiology addendum reaches referrer; PT episode produces signed discharge and referral closure; ambiguous prescription transmission reconciles without duplication; payment and refund replay reproduces balances.

- [ ] S-G4-07 · G4 gate evidence and Product Owner acceptance (G4).

## G5 — launch and operations

Gate evidence: each site approves workflow, release policy, market constraints, integrations, identity procedures, staffing and downtime drills; messaging units verify eligibility, ownership, after-hours guidance and backup coverage; no unresolved isolation, record-integrity or critical-escalation defects.

- [ ] S-G5-01 · Market policy pack, hosting region, jurisdiction and data handling map (OPS-01, PRD-05).
- [ ] S-G5-02 · Clinical templates, code sets, interpreting privileges and result escalation approvals (ADM-01).
- [ ] S-G5-03 · Result release rules, sensitive information handling and identity recovery approvals (OPS-01).
- [ ] S-G5-04 · Laboratory, PACS and pharmacy interface contracts, credentials and outage drills (OPS-01).
- [ ] S-G5-12 · Per-site launch approvals and final G5 acceptance (G5).

## Cross-cutting contracts

Delivered inside the stories above, not scheduled separately.

## Improvement ideas

Raised by the dispatch-3 run-3 verification. Address in the next authorized change to the owning file.

## One-week execution plan (1 wave per hour)

Created 2026-11-19T08:55Z from the open entries above. Horizon: 7 days × 24 hours = 168 hourly wave slots. This plan uses 7 implementation waves; the remaining 161 hourly slots are buffer for `needs-fix` retries, fix PRs, gate re-runs and human approvals.

Cadence and limits:

- One wave is launched per hour at minute 7 (`swarm.yml` schedule `cron: '7 * * * *'`). Because the `agent-swarm` concurrency group queues (`cancel-in-progress: false`, `queue: max`), a wave starts when the previous one finishes.
- Up to 10 workers per wave, one task per worker. Each task targets 50 minutes or less so a wave fits its hour; the 175-minute agent timeout is a hard cap, not a target.
- A wave takes a task only after its `depends` are `[x]`; gate entries wait for their phase tasks to merge.
- S-G0-04 is blocked (search, files, workers and exports surfaces do not exist yet) and is not scheduled.
- Gate entries (S-G1-09, S-G2-11, S-G3-13, S-G4-07, S-G5-12) prepare evidence only. Product Owner, clinical and privacy acceptance are human decisions; a worker cannot satisfy them.
- G5 production enablement additionally needs signed site configuration and real partner contracts. The swarm can only produce synthetic evidence.

| Wave | Hour | Tasks (one per worker) | Gate / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | H+1 | `X-01`, `X-02`, `X-03`, `X-04`, `IMP-04`, `S-G0-06`, `S-G0-07`, `S-G0-08` | G0 identity and shared contracts; IMP-04 CI fix |
| W2 | H+2 | `S-G1-02`, `S-G1-03`, `S-G1-04`, `S-G1-05`, `S-G1-06`, `S-G1-07`, `S-G1-08` | G1 clinic workflows and documentation |
| W3 | H+3 | `S-G1-09`, `S-G2-01`, `S-G2-02`, `S-G2-03`, `S-G2-04`, `S-G2-05`, `S-G2-06`, `S-G2-07`, `S-G2-08` | G1 gate evidence, then G2 orders and exchange core |
| W4 | H+4 | `S-G2-09`, `S-G2-10`, `S-G2-11`, `S-G3-01`, `S-G3-02`, `S-G3-03`, `S-G3-04`, `S-G3-05`, `S-G3-06`, `S-G3-07` | G2 lab, conformance and gate evidence; patient access begins |
| W5 | H+5 | `S-G3-08`, `S-G3-09`, `S-G3-10`, `S-G3-11`, `S-G3-12`, `S-G3-13`, `S-G4-01`, `S-G4-02`, `S-G4-03`, `S-G4-04` | Patient/messaging completion and G3 gate; specialty intake begins |

  - scope: scripts/swarm.py, scripts/tests/test_swarm_delivery_state.py
  - details:
    1. Read how the integrator decides whether a pull request has current-head Delivery evidence (search `scripts/swarm.py` for `Delivery`, `statusCheckRollup` and the run listing) and `.github/workflows/delivery.yml`.
    2. Add `delivery_state(runs, head_sha)` returning exactly one of `passed`, `failed`, `pending`, `missing` or `approval-required` for the current head SHA (a run for an older SHA is `missing`; a run waiting for a first-time-contributor approval or an environment gate is `approval-required`; cancelled counts as `failed`; skipped Markdown-only runs follow the existing documentation rule). Use it in the integrator so only `passed` (or the documented documentation exception) merges, `pending` waits without a label, `failed` goes to the fix workers, and `missing` or `approval-required` asks for a run and never merges.
    3. Tests: each of the five states, an older-SHA run, a re-run that supersedes a failure, and the documentation exception. Scripts are protected files: the swarm may now merge them (the integrator opens an oversight issue). Keep the change small and covered by tests.
    If you cannot finish because something you need is missing, write what is missing under `## Why this is not finished` in your notes and stop; do not guess.

The result is a measured, clause-by-clause view of how much of the specification is built.
